This comparison outlines the standardized Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification codes for direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). These specific codes are utilized for quality measurement and tracking in the clinical treatment of atrial fibrillation [^src1]. Because the data represents a categorical mapping rather than quantitative performance metrics, there are no numerical leaders, trailers, targets, or temporal trends to evaluate; the table simply establishes the foundational coding framework required to monitor these prescriptions.

The registry tracks four specific DOAC medications under this framework. The first is [[b01ae07|B01AE07]], which corresponds to dabigatran [^src1]. The remaining three belong to the B01AF subgroup: [[b01af01|B01AF01]] for rivaroxaban, [[b01af02|B01AF02]] for apixaban, and [[b01af03|B01AF03]] for edoxaban [^src1]. Together, these four codes encompass the primary direct oral anticoagulants monitored in the quality assurance data.
